voice.note: speaker → script/cast.json (voice, speed, pitch). Per line: speed (× the speaker's), pre/post (ms of silence before/after the voice), say (what is spoken, if not `text`), estVoice (s: the predicted voice length, tools/estimate.py; replaced by the real voice once tools/voice.py has run).

source: Mahabharata, Critical Edition (BORI), Adi Parva, Shakuntala sub-parva. CHECKED AGAINST CE 1.65.12–42 and 1.66.1–17, 1.67.1 (GRETIL e-text of the constituted text, lab/ce; star passages and appendix lines are apparatus and were not used; Ganguli (vulgate) only as a reading aid): the king asks who she is and whose (1.65.12–13: `asked`); she is held to be Kanva's daughter (1.65.15); he: the holy one is a celibate; how are you his daughter (1.65.16–17: the hook); she tells what she heard Kanva tell a seer who asked about her birth (1.65.18–19: `said`; the whole tale is hers, at second hand); Vishvamitra's great austerity troubled Indra, lord of the gods, who feared to be shaken from his seat (1.65.20–21: `tapas`); Indra tells Menaka, who excels the apsarases in divine qualities, to tempt him and hinder his austerity (1.65.22–26: `sent`); she is afraid of his anger and his power and asks that the Wind and the god of love go with her (1.65.27–42; in the picture, not voiced); she plays before the seer and the wind carries off her garment (1.66.1–4; not shown); he sees her, desires her and invites her; she is willing; they live together a long time as if it were a day (1.66.5–7: `saw`); he begets Shakuntala on her on a ridge of the Himalaya by the river Malini (1.66.8); Menaka leaves the new-born by the Malini and goes quickly to Indra's court, her task done (1.66.9: `left`, the turn); in that lonely forest full of lions and tigers, birds (shakunta) surround the child so that no flesh-eater may harm her (1.66.10–11: `birds`); Kanva, going to bathe, sees her lying surrounded by birds, brings her home and makes her his daughter (1.66.12: `found`); because she was guarded by shakuntas he named her Shakuntala (1.66.14: `name`); she knows no other father (1.66.17); the king: be my wife (1.67.1: the cliffhanger). The CE does not say the birds fed her or sheltered her with their wings, only that they stood round and guarded her: the picture shows a ring of birds. Indra and the king are on plaques, not named in the voice (the names-per-10-s rule).
structure: As from episode 41 (script/ARC-41-50.md, script/ARC-51-60.md): COLD OPEN (≤ 8 words; the hook style rotates and never repeats the episode before; no episode of this batch opens on fire) → title (hook post) → STORY from ≈ 4.5 s with the UNVOICED recap band → the episode stands alone (every name has an identifier in "names", shown as a plaque) → one question closed (loop.answeredBy), the previous one answered by 15 s (loop.prevAnsweredBy) → turn at 40–60 % after a real silence, a second silence where the story allows → one face close-up with a change of emotion → one signature shot → the cliffhanger with the source line → a ≤ 1.2 s NEXT › band that dissolves into frame 1. Per line: pal (the colour script: no hue for more than two lines), cam (≥ 4 distinct moves), tr (transitions born from the medium), amb / foley / music (three sound layers; ambLead / ambLag = J- and L-cuts). Gate: tools/gate.mjs.

names.Menaka: an apsara, a nymph of heaven

loop.hookQuestion: How can a celibate sage have a daughter?
loop.prevQuestion: How can a celibate sage have a daughter?
loop.openQuestion: Will she marry a king she has only just met?

strings.recapLine: King Dushyanta, alone in a forest hermitage, met a young woman.

lines.text: How can a celibate sage have a daughter?
lines.say: How can a celibate sage [p:60] have a daughter?
lines.note: COLD OPEN (a question card; no fire): from high above, a river bank: a tiny bundle on the grass, ringed by a great wheel of birds of every kind, standing wing to wing. A crane down toward it. The card in the upper third.

lines.text: A king asked a young hermit woman who she was.
lines.say: A king asked a young hermit woman [p:100] who she was.
lines.note: STORY 0 with the unvoiced recap band (top): the hermitage yard: the king seated on a grass seat, plainly dressed (plaque: Dushyanta · a king of Puru's line), the girl standing three paces off with a water jar; a slow track.

lines.speaker: shakuntala
lines.text: "People call me the sage Kanva's daughter. Hear why."
lines.say: People call me the sage Kanva's daughter. [p:260] Hear why.
lines.note: STORY 1 · THE CLOSE-UP: her face fills the frame: a smile, then the look turns inward and grave as she begins (the gaze drops and goes far).

lines.text: Long ago, the penance of another sage frightened the king of the gods.
lines.say: Long ago, [p:100] the penance of another sage [p:100] frightened the king of the gods.
lines.note: STORY 2 · NEW LIGHT (dharma-copper): a tilt up: a gaunt ascetic standing motionless on one leg, arms raised, heat shimmering off him (plaque: Vishvamitra · a king turned fierce ascetic); high above, on a cloud throne, a crowned god gripping the arms of his seat (plaque: Indra · king of the gods).

lines.text: He sent Menaka, a nymph of heaven, to break it.
lines.say: He sent Menaka, [p:100] a nymph of heaven, [p:150] to break it.
lines.note: STORY 3 · NEW LIGHT (crystal-sky): Indra's bright court: Menaka, pearl-aqua, a diadem, before the throne; she hesitates, a hand to her throat (the text: she fears the sage's anger); then steps off the cloud's edge, the wind's long scarves round her (plaque: Menaka · an apsara, a nymph of heaven; sub: the finest of them · Adi 1.65.22).

lines.text: Vishvamitra desired her; and she was willing.
lines.say: Vishvamitra desired her; [p:250] and she was willing.
lines.note: STORY 4 (hermitage-green): a rack focus from blowing leaves and her scarf in the foreground (the wind is her ally: the text has it) to the ascetic, far, whose raised arms slowly come down as he turns his head. The two are never drawn touching; a full clearing lies between them.

lines.text: By a river, a daughter was born. Menaka left her there, and went back to heaven.
lines.say: By a river, [p:80] a daughter was born. [p:350] Menaka left her there, [p:150] and went back to heaven.
lines.note: STORY 5 · THE TURN (≈ 45 %) after a real silence · NEW LIGHT (riverbank-pearl): Menaka kneels and lays a swaddled new-born on the grass by the water (a swaddled infant, never a standing child); she rises, does not look back, and a tilt up follows her into the pale sky until she is a point of light (plaque: Malini · a river of the foothills). The word of the turn: ALONE.

lines.text: In a forest of lions and tigers, birds ringed the child and kept her safe.
lines.say: In a forest [p:60] of lions and tigers, [p:200] birds ringed the child [p:100] and kept her safe.
lines.note: STORY 6 · THE SIGNATURE SHOT (venom-violet: dusk in the wood): frame-within-frame, through dark leaves: two pairs of eyes and a tiger's striped shoulder in the foreground shade; beyond, in a pool of last light, the infant ringed by birds standing wing to wing, herons, parrots, geese, a peacock, more dropping in from above. The beasts do not come nearer.

lines.text: The sage Kanva found her, and raised her as his own.
lines.say: The sage Kanva [p:80] found her, [p:200] and raised her as his own.
lines.note: STORY 7 · NEW LIGHT (island-gold: morning; answers the hook): an old sage with a water-pot, come to bathe, stops; the birds part; he kneels and lifts the infant in both arms (plaque: Kanva · a great sage).

lines.speaker: shakuntala
lines.text: "Guarded by birds, by shakuntas: so he named me Shakuntala."
lines.say: Guarded by birds, [p:100] by shakuntas: [p:260] so he named me Shakuntala.
lines.note: STORY 8 (a second real silence before it): the yard again: she stands with a hand lifted and a small bird alights on it; others on the thatch behind her (plaque: SHAKUNTALA · "guarded by birds"). A slow orbit.

lines.text: The king listened. A king's daughter, then, he said: be my wife.
lines.say: The king listened. [p:350] A king's daughter, then, [p:100] he said: [p:200] be my wife.
lines.note: NEXT 1 (the catalog's cliffhanger; CE 1.67.1): the light gone to late coral: the king rises from the grass seat, a hand held out, palm up; she, three paces off, has gone very still, the bird flown. The source line (top).
The NEXT › band over the cliffhanger image, with the source line; dissolve into frame 1.
